children: The distribution-per-unit of Singapore small-to-mid-cap real-estate investment trusts could accelerate in 2H, say DBS Group Research analysts in a note. They cite factors such as a smaller base and more pronounced benefits from declining financing costs, noting Singapore's broadly lower interest-rate benchmark. They expect small-to-mid-cap REIT DPUs to accelerate around 4% sequentially in 2H, compared with a roughly 1% growth estimate for large caps. The overall sector's DPU is likely to grow at around 3% on average on year in 2026, they add. DBS's REIT segment pecking order is office, industrial, retail and hospitality. The bank's preferred names include Centurion Accommodation REIT and NTT DC REIT. (megan.cheah@wsj.com)
